decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up right-arm approach; key lies in right workspace, angled from the reference. Keep left arm parked.
Continue curved elbow-up approach with open right gripper, adding yaw to match the visible key angle.
Move toward the key from above, rotating right tool downward while preserving the current elbow-up branch.
Finish downward alignment over the key shaft, retaining clearance until wrist imagery confirms the grasp location.
Use wrist view to center the key between the open jaws; small lateral and yaw corrections before closing.
Refine shaft centering from wrist RGB and partially close to inspect jaw placement before grasping.
Close around the centered shaft and make a short test lift, checking visual retention rather than gripper command state.
Key appears retained between right jaws. Lift clear of the table while starting gradual yaw toward the handover pose.
Raise the retained key toward handover height, yaw gradually, and begin the left elbow-up receiving approach with ample separation.
Key is no longer retained in wrist RGB. Open and descend cautiously for a new grasp; hold the left arm clear while the key settles.
Re-approach the settled key's new position and angle, with open jaws and a gradual descent; previous grasp slipped.
Center nearer the key's lower shaft and lower toward contact height. Correct the remaining angle from wrist RGB before closing.
Set the jaws slightly lower around the shaft, center laterally, and close without lifting yet to check a firmer grasp.
Allow the closing command to settle at fixed pose before attempting any lift; verify shaft contact visually.
Maintain full closure longer, then make an 8 mm vertical retention test without rotating the key.
Lift slowly with no yaw, maintaining closure and checking that the key remains fixed relative to the jaws.
The key is pivoting at a tooth-side grasp. Set it down and shift toward the ring for a lower-shaft grasp that better preserves orientation.
Align the lower shaft between the jaws using the now-clear wrist view, then start closing gradually with the key still supported.
Finish yaw alignment and close around the lower shaft rather than the teeth; keep the key supported until the jaws settle.
The shaft is now centered cleanly between the jaws. Lift vertically with closure maintained while the left arm continues its separated elbow-up approach.
Key remains fixed in the right jaws. Raise and yaw it toward a central handover while advancing the left arm along a continuous elbow-up approach.
Complete right-hand presentation at safe height, keeping the key clamped. Continue orienting the open left receiver without crossing arms.
Hold the visually retained key steady in the right hand. Bring the open left hand closer with a sideways receiving orientation, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Complete the left receiving orientation while leaving a gap to the key; right hand stays fixed and closed.
Replan from the executed prefix with smaller receiving-pose increments after the continuity rejection; narrow the left opening while still separated from the ring.
Advance the left receiver along its own tool axis toward the exposed key ring; hold the right grasp and retain a small approach margin.
Fine approach to the exposed ring with a slight height correction from the left wrist; start narrowing the receiver while the right still supports the key.
Seat the left fingers slightly farther over the ring and close to establish the receiving grasp before any right-hand release.
Left wrist shows the ring seated between its fingers. Keep left fully closed and gradually release the right hand without moving either arm.
Withdraw the open right gripper laterally in its own workspace; keep the left ring grasp fixed and inspect transfer retention.
Transfer remains visually retained by the left ring grasp. Begin the continuous elbow-up rotation toward an upright key while parking the open right hand farther right.
Continue raising and pitching the left-held key toward vertical along the same elbow-up branch. Park the right arm clear of the insertion area.
Replan from the continuity interruption using smaller left rotations and translations; maintain the ring grasp and the elbow-up branch.
Continue the left-held key's upward arc toward the lock, with small continuous pitch changes and the right arm stationary.
Move the left-held key toward the lock while finishing its upright orientation and adapting yaw to the visible slot direction.
The ring has shifted at the left fingertips. Stop rotation and attempt a deeper reseating of the ring with a small forward/downward adjustment before continuing.
The key slipped free of the left grasp. Raise and clear the left gripper to locate its resting position for recovery, keeping the right arm parked.
Approach the visible key ring beside the lock with open left jaws, retaining clearance to inspect its settled orientation before regrasping.
Lower the left jaws toward the exposed upright ring beside the lock, correcting laterally from wrist RGB and keeping a moderate opening.
Ring is centered between the left jaws. Stop descent after possible rim contact, ease upward slightly, and close at the observed pose to regrasp it.
The ring is seated cleanly again. Lift the upright key above the lock and translate toward the visible slot, preserving orientation and full closure.
Pause above the lock with the ring clamped to assess the key's changing orientation before attempting slot alignment.
The recovered key is retained but its shaft is sideways. Begin a slow pivot about the held ring to bring the shaft downward, compensating EE position and staying in the left workspace.
Continue the ring-centered pivot toward a downward shaft, adding modest yaw for the slot and translating the held ring toward the lock without crossing arms.
Slowly pivot about the grasped ring along the key's plane, keeping its height nearly fixed and checking retention while bringing the shaft closer to vertical.
Continue the ring-centered pitch in smaller increments, removing a little sideways tilt. Keep the retained key clear of the slot until its shaft is vertical.
The ring has moved to the fingertip edges while the shaft is supported near the lock. Stop pitching and regrasp noticeably deeper over the ring before lifting again.
Replan from the unchanged observation after the rejected approach. Use smaller forward increments to seat the ring farther inside the open left fingers.
The key has slipped beside the lock. Recenter the open left jaws on the visible ring with small lateral motion, keeping the current continuous arm configuration.
The key is flat beside the lock, outside the fingers. Clear upward and unwind the left wrist toward a top-down recovery approach, preserving elbow-up continuity.
Move above the now-visible key in the left workspace, continuing to unwind toward a top-down shaft grasp with ample table clearance.
Complete the downward approach orientation and move over the left-side key, keeping jaws open and using wrist alignment rather than the prior slipped grasp.
Approach the key ring from above, moving along the visible key axis and lowering gradually. Plan a ring grasp that permits an outward, elbow-up upright rotation.
Center and seat the ring deeper in the left jaw pads using the wrist view, then partially close for inspection at table height.
Adjust from the lower shaft onto the ring itself, then close slowly at fixed height for a deeper, centered ring grasp.
Let the ring grasp settle under full closure, then make a short vertical lift to verify retention before any rotation.
The key is securely visible in a lower-shaft grasp. Lift clear before rotating in the outward direction that keeps the left arm in its own workspace.
Pivot the retained key outward about the grasp so its shaft points down, compensating wrist position while translating the key toward the lock.
Continue the smooth outward pivot and approach toward the lock; the key remains stable relative to the left jaws.
Continue controlled outward pitch with compensated grasp height; keep the shaft above the lock and the left arm elbow-up.
Bring the shaft closer to vertical while preserving the stable lower-shaft grasp and a small height clearance over the slot.
Finish most of the upright pitch with small compensated increments, aligning the held shaft toward the visible lock while leaving clearance before insertion.
